t:
(a) 
Except as provided in subsection (b) and in section 305, the maximum part of the aggregate disposable earnings of an individual for any workweek which is subjected to garnishment may not exceed

        (1) 
25 per centum of his disposable earnings for that week, or
 
        (2) 
the amount by which his disposable earnings for that week exceed thirty times the Federal minimum hourly wage prescribed by section 6(a)(1) of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 in effect at the time the earnings are payable,
   whichever is less. In the case of earnings for any pay period other than a week, the Secretary of Labor shall by regulation prescribe a multiple of the Federal minimum hourly wage equivalent in effect to that set forth in paragraph (2).

    (b) 
The restrictions of subsection (a) do not apply in the case of

        (1) 
any order of any court for the support, of any person.
 
        (2) 
any order of any court of bankruptcy under chapter XIII of the Bankruptcy Act.
 
        (3) 
any debt due for any State or Federal tax.
  
    (c) 
No court of the United States or any State may make, execute, or enforce any order or process in violation of this section.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is purely a substantive limit on garnishment with no outside-party process, so the answer is No. However, the section directs the Secretary of Labor to act "by regulation," and under the definition a requirement or authorization of rulemaking counts as participation because rulemaking brings the public into the federal decision. The court-order references in subsections (b) and (c) only restrict courts and do not themselves create participation, so the label rests on the rulemaking mandate.
fable.s: the Secretary of Labor shall by regulation prescribe a multiple of the Federal minimum hourly wage equivalent in effect to that set forth in paragraph (2)

qwen_block.w: This section establishes statutory limits on wage garnishment and exceptions for support orders, bankruptcy, and taxes. It does not require consultation with outside parties, public comment, or advisory boards. The mention of the Secretary of Labor prescribing regulations is an internal agency action to define technical equivalents, not a participatory process involving the public or outside entities. There is no mechanism for outside participation in the decision-making process described here.
qwen_block.s: In the case of earnings for any pay period other than a week, the Secretary of Labor shall by regulation prescribe a multiple of the Federal minimum hourly wage equivalent in effect to that set forth in paragraph (2).

opus.w: The statute requires the Secretary of Labor to act by regulation. Under the definition and Example 6, required rulemaking counts as participation because it brings in public comment. It is tempting to answer No because the section mostly sets garnishment limits and names no outside consultee, but the rulemaking requirement alone meets the definition. The court-order and exemption provisions do not give anyone a right to sue, so they do not affect the label either way.
opus.s: In the case of earnings for any pay period other than a week, the Secretary of Labor shall by regulation prescribe a multiple of the Federal minimum hourly wage equivalent in effect to that set forth in paragraph (2).
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** This section reads like a plain cap on wage garnishment, and no outside party is named as being consulted. That reading fails because the definition counts "requiring rulemaking" as participation. Example 6 also says that giving an agency regulation authority counts. Here the statute says the Secretary of Labor "shall by regulation prescribe" the equivalent multiple for pay periods other than a week. Rulemaking brings in public notice and comment, which crosses the federal boundary.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes limits on wage garnishment and exceptions for support, bankruptcy, and taxes. While it authorizes the Secretary of Labor to prescribe regulations for non-weekly pay periods, this is an internal administrative determination of a mathematical equivalent, not a participatory process involving consultation with outside parties, public comment, or advisory boards. There is no involvement of non-federal entities in the decision-making process described here.
qwen_chat.s: In the case of earnings for any pay period other than a week, the Secretary of Labor shall by regulation prescribe a multiple of the Federal minimum hourly wage equivalent in effect to that set forth in paragraph (2).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretary of Labor prescribing regulations involves participation because it is a rulemaking process. However, the definition explicitly states that "requiring rulemaking" is a form of participation, but this section merely authorizes the Secretary to prescribe a mathematical equivalent for pay periods other than weeks. More importantly, the core of the section is about limiting garnishment amounts and exceptions for support, bankruptcy, and taxes. There is no requirement for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards in this specific text. The Secretary's action is an internal administrative calculation/definition, not a participatory process with outsiders. The section does not mention consulting with states, tribes, the public, or experts. It does not grant a right to sue. It does not involve an advisory committee with non-federal members. Therefore, it is "No".
